notes: Rupiah amounts now read correctly: a receipt printed Rp 74.000 is saved as seventy-four thousand, not 74. If a month has no spending in your workspace’s currency, the home screen says so and tells you how many receipts are in another currency, instead of showing $0. If you leave to confirm your email while creating a YourTal account, coming back now finishes signing you in, and tax totals use your workspace’s own tax name.

This build is signed with Snap Apps’ own private key instead of the shared test key, so Android will not install it over your current app. Before updating, open the app and let any snaps still waiting send, then uninstall Snap Apps and install this version from the download page. You only need to do this once; later updates install over it as before.

Each snap is one page, and a scan needs a credit. When credits run out the app says so and offers to buy more; snaps already sent are kept and read once you have credits again. Buying credits now goes through a card checkout (simulated on this test build, so no real money moves). Settings can delete your account, and the trip recorder explains why it asks for your location before Android does.

You can now sign in or create an account with YourTal, and link YourTal so receipts scanned with bought credits earn points. Each scan uses one credit, free ones first, and a scan we cannot read gives its credit back. Amounts now show in your workspace’s own currency, so an Indonesian workspace reads in Rupiah (Rp). Credit prices stay in Australian dollars, because that is what Snap Apps charges.

You can now reset a forgotten password by email, and a new account confirms its email address. Sessions now expire, so after a long time away you may be asked to sign in again, and Settings can sign you out on every device at once. Help now shows your version and build, so a problem report says which one you have.

Snap Apps has a new look: a bar along the bottom of every screen with Scan raised in the middle, white cards and a new typeface. A photo you take with no signal is kept on your phone and sent when you are back online. Settings now shows your version and build, and the update card tells you what is new. Screens that are not finished yet, such as the wallet, alerts and rewards, are hidden for now.
